description: We are a passionate, innovation-driven team exploring the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and space research. Our focus is on analysing microgravity combustion data to uncover meaningful patterns and develop data-driven insights for improved fire safety. We welcome teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, data analytics, scientific research, physics, data visualization, and software development who are eager to collaborate and build impactful solutions.
summary:
On Earth, NASA-STD-6001B certifies spacecraft materials using a six-inch vertical flame test governed by buoyancy-driven convection—where hot exhaust rises and pulls fresh oxygen into the flame. In microgravity (0g) and lunar gravity (0.16g), buoyancy vanishes, creating a critical fire-safety blind spot: flames collapse into oxygen-starved spheres sustained by subtle cabin ventilation, while low-temperature "cool flames" burn invisibly to the naked eye.

IGNIS-0G is an interactive microgravity combustion and spacecraft certification simulator grounded in 16 empirical flight datasets and 24 investigations from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. Engineers and students can test materials across Earth, Lunar, and ISS cabin atmospheres (including Artemis 34% O2 / 56.5 kPa conditions), visualize real-time Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) U-curves, inspect invisible FLEX droplet cool flames via a simulated Thermal IR camera, audit flight certification margins, and query a NASA PSI citation copilot—complete with a hands-free 6-act Autopilot simulation.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

IGNIS-0G bridges the gap between standard 1g terrestrial material screening and real low-gravity spacecraft fire behavior through six interactive telemetry modules:

1. Gravity & Buoyancy Morphing: Compares 1.00g Earth teardrop flames against 0.16g Lunar and 0.00g orbital spherical diffusion flames.

2. Cabin Atmosphere & U-Curve Oscilloscope: Models Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) and flame spread rates across varying O2 percentages, cabin pressures (kPa), and forced ventilation airflows (cm/s), including the Artemis Exploration Atmosphere (34% O2, 56.5 kPa).

3. Six-Inch Material Strip Burn Test: Benchmarks aerospace polymers and fabrics (Nomex, Kapton, Ultem, Silicone, Cotton) against NASA-STD-6001B pass/fail thresholds.

4. Lunar Certification Audit: Evaluates multi-zone bulkhead safety margins before clearing a cabin configuration for lunar flight.

5. Thermal IR Cool-Flame & Smoke Aerosol Detection: Toggles an infrared camera mode to expose low-temperature alkane cool flames (FLEX) invisible to standard optical sensors, paired with smoke particulate sizing (SAME).

6. NASA PSI Research Copilot & 6-Act Autopilot: Ranks citations across 24 NASA PSI flight investigations and provides a one-click "Run Simulation" virtual-cursor tour for rapid judge evaluation.

BENEFITS, IMPACT & CREATIVITY

- Replaces static PDF tables with a tactile, real-time mission telemetry deck so engineers, safety reviewers, and students can immediately see why materials passing Earth tests can fail in enriched-oxygen lunar cabins.

- Combines deterministic empirical physics equations with a zero-dependency retro-CRT GameBoy interface and hands-free virtual cursor demo.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & ACCESSIBILITY / COST FACTORS

- Tech Stack: Zero-dependency Vanilla JavaScript (ES6 Modules), HTML5 Canvas 2D physics rendering, Web Audio API telemetry synthesis, and custom CSS3 styling.

- Cost & Accessibility: 100% browser-based with zero backend server costs, sub-second load times, offline-capable empirical JSON datasets, and keyboard/screen-friendly tactile controls.

- Live App: https://ignis-dusky.vercel.app/ | Source Code & Physics Whitepaper: https://github.com/Awwad-007/IGNIS
